steps.title: Model 5-mark answer
steps.body:
**Q. Explain any five features of the Indian Constitution's Preamble.**
Intro: The Preamble states the values on which the Constitution is based.
1. Sovereign — independent of external control.
2. Socialist — reduce inequalities.
3. Secular — no official religion.
4. Democratic republic — elected rulers and elected head of state.
5. Justice, liberty, equality, fraternity — the goals for citizens.
Conclusion: These values guide all laws and institutions.

steps.title: Frequent confusions
steps.body:
- MSP (to farmers) vs issue price (to consumers).
- Adopted 26 Nov vs in force 26 Jan.
- Seasonal vs disguised unemployment.
- 84 SC vs 47 ST seats.

cards.front: Rajya Sabha can delay a money bill by…

cards.back: 100 days of wage work per rural household per year
75% rural, 50% urban; 5 kg per person per month

cards.front: Heart and soul of the Constitution (Ambedkar)

quiz.q: The 42nd Amendment added:
quiz.why: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added the words 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble. 'Sovereign', 'republic' and 'justice' were already in the original text.

quiz.q: Who appoints the CEC?
quiz.why: The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President of India. After appointment, the CEC works independently of the government.

quiz.q: Working capital example:
quiz.why: Seeds are working capital because they are used up in a single crop cycle. Buildings, tubewells and tractors last many years, so they are fixed capital.

quiz.q: AAY gives poorest families:
quiz.why: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) each poorest family gets 35 kg of grain per month at a very low price. The 5 kg per person figure is for NFSA.

quiz.q: How many Fundamental Rights?
quiz.why: India has six Fundamental Rights: equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies. The right to property was removed.

lessons.title: Mock Paper 1 walkthrough (mixed)

scenes.text: Neha reads the whole paper in the first 5 minutes and marks easy questions.
She answers MCQs fast, then case-based, then long answers, leaving 10 minutes to check.

steps.title: Time plan for an 80-mark paper (3 hours)
steps.body:
- Read paper: 10 min
- MCQs (20 × 1): 20 min
- Very short / short answers: 45 min
- Long answers (5 marks): 60 min
- Case-based: 25 min
- Map: 10 min
- Revision: 10 min

steps.title: Solved case-based question
steps.body:
**Case**: 'In Palampur, Savita borrowed ₹3,000 at 24% interest for four months and agreed to work on the lender's field at ₹100 a day during harvest.'
(a) Who is the lender likely to be? → A large landowner (Tejpal Singh). (1)
(b) Calculate the interest. → 3,000 × 0.24 × 4/12 = ₹240. (1)
(c) Why is this arrangement unfair? → High interest plus forced cheap labour; small farmers lack access to bank credit. (2)

steps.title: Solved source-based question
steps.body:
**Source**: 'Let him read the newspaper aloud in the café; let the shopkeepers argue.' (based on 18th-century France)
(a) What spread revolutionary ideas? → Books, pamphlets, newspapers read aloud in salons and coffee-houses. (1)
(b) Name two thinkers whose ideas were discussed. → Rousseau, Montesquieu. (1)
(c) Why did these ideas appeal to the middle class? → They rejected privilege by birth and supported merit and rights. (2)

steps.title: Exam-day mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing more than needed for 1-mark questions.
- Not reading 'any two' / 'any three' instructions.
- Leaving map labels unclear.

activity.prompt: Before submitting your paper, check:
items: All questions attempted, including internal choices
Question numbers written correctly
Calculations shown in steps
Map items labelled clearly
Key dates and names underlined

quiz.q: In a 3-mark answer you should write:
quiz.why: A 3-mark answer is usually expected to have three distinct points, one for each mark. One long sentence or ten points do not match the marks.

quiz.q: The best first step in an exam is to:
quiz.why: The best first step in an exam is to read the whole paper and plan your time. This avoids wasting time on a hard question at the start.

quiz.q: Interest on ₹3,000 at 24% for 4 months:
quiz.why: Simple interest = 3,000 × 24/100 × 4/12 = ₹240. The rate is per year, so 4 months is 4/12 of a year.

quiz.q: For a case-based question, answers should:
options: Use facts from the case and the chapter
quiz.why: In a case-based question, use facts from the case and link them to concepts from the chapter. Copying the case or ignoring it will not earn full marks.

quiz.q: How much time to keep for revision at the end?
quiz.why: Keep about 10 minutes at the end of the exam to revise, so you can correct mistakes and fill gaps. Two hours or one hour would be more than the exam allows.

questions.q: Mock 1 · The Third Estate included:
questions.why: The Third Estate included everyone outside the clergy and nobility: peasants, artisans, merchants and lawyers. The clergy were the First Estate and nobles the Second.

questions.q: Mock 1 · The highest peak of peninsular India:
questions.why: Anai Mudi (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai hills is the highest peak of peninsular India. The other peaks are lower.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Voting age in India:
questions.why: The voting age in India is 18. It was 21 until 1988 and was then lowered by an amendment.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Food security includes:
questions.why: Food security has three dimensions: availability of food, accessibility to it, and affordability. Production, imports or prices alone do not ensure it.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Kristallnacht took place in:
questions.why: Kristallnacht, the 'Night of Broken Glass', took place in November 1938, when Jewish homes and shops were attacked in Germany.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Which is correct?
questions.why: The loo is a hot, dry summer wind of north India. October heat comes after the monsoon, mango showers are in Kerala and Karnataka, and kaal baisakhi is in West Bengal.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Assertion (A): The judiciary is independent. Reason (R): Judges can be removed only by impeachment by two-thirds of each House.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: Both statements are true. Judges can be removed only by an impeachment needing two-thirds in each House, which makes removal very difficult, so they can act independently. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Mock 1 · Case: A Gaddi family moves from the Shiwaliks to Lahul and Spiti in April. Why?
options: Low hills dry up; high meadows have fresh pasture after snowmelt
questions.why: In summer the low hills dry up while the high meadows have fresh grass after the snow melts, so Gaddis move to Lahul and Spiti. It is not for taxes or floods.

questions.q: Mock 2 · The Constitution was adopted on:
questions.why: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. 9 December 1946 was the first Constituent Assembly meeting.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Disguised unemployment is mostly found in:
questions.why: Disguised unemployment is mostly found in agriculture, where more family members work on a farm than needed. Banking, IT and mining do not have it.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Which tributary joins the Ganga at Prayagraj?
questions.why: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. The Kosi, Son and Gandak join the Ganga at other points.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Assertion (A): The Weimar Republic was unstable. Reason (R): Proportional representation and Article 48 weakened it.
questions.why: Both are true. Proportional representation produced unstable coalitions and Article 48 let the President suspend rights and rule by decree, both weaknesses of the Weimar Republic. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Mock 2 · A district has 8,00,000 people in 400 sq km. Density?
questions.why: Density = population ÷ area = 800,000 ÷ 400 = 2,000 persons per sq km.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Rural family of 5 earns ₹4,000/month. Using ₹816/person, are they poor?
questions.why: The family poverty line = 5 × ₹816 = ₹4,080 per month. Their income of ₹4,000 is below that, so they are poor.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Time difference between 82°30'E and 0°:
questions.why: The Earth rotates 1° in 4 minutes, so 82.5° × 4 = 330 minutes = 5 hours 30 minutes. This is the difference between IST and GMT.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Case: In 1917 women in bread queues start strikes, soldiers join, and the ruler abdicates without any party leading. Which revolution and what came next?
questions.why: Women in bread queues striking, soldiers joining and the Tsar abdicating with no party in the lead describe the February Revolution of 1917. The Provisional Government then took over.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Case: A tribal village's forest becomes a reserved forest; shifting cultivation is banned; villagers must work free to stay. Which historical case is closest?
questions.why: Reserved forests, the ban on shifting cultivation and forced free work in forest villages match the case of Bastar, where the 1905 proposal to reserve forests led to the 1910 rebellion.

questions.q: Mock 2 · Which set is fully correct?
questions.why: The correct years are MGNREGA 2005, NFSA 2013, RTI 2005 and NHRC 1993. The other sets give wrong years.
